prior_summary: Manipulated-object-equivariant Cartesian targets use blue during predecessor release and red during approach, grasp, lift, carry, place and retreat, selected causally by nearest 3D TCP distance.
applicable_conditions: Prefer when buffered red is displaced or yawed but remains observable, table-supported, collision-free and reachable. The early declared entry is supported when TCP is still nearer blue; typed arguments must identify red, red_goal and blue.
termination_guidance: Use only the unchanged framework success expression red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal. Demonstrated open gripper and high TCP retreat are continuation guidance, not extra success requirements.
limitations: Nearest-object switching can be discontinuous and does not infer contact. Pose noise, missed grasps, slips, unstable blue, unreachable displacement and unseen collisions are not solved; demonstrations do not establish recovery.
